column1: As Figure 13-11 shows, these two shifts cause income to rise and the currency to depreciate. This analysis has an important implication: expectations about the exchange rate are partially self-fulfilling. For example, suppose that for some reason people reduce their expectations of the future value of the Mexican peso. Investors will place a larger risk premium on Mexican assets: u will rise in Mexico. This expectation will drive up Mexican interest rates and, as we have just seen, will drive down the value of the Mexican currency. Thus, the expectation that a currency will lose value in the future causes it to lose value today.
